title: "Building the cohort"

This script builds the study cohort: one row per person, each with their index cryptococcosis hospitalization. It follows the steps in §4 of the [analysis plan](analysis-plan.qmd#4-study-population), and every exclusion goes through the cohort flowchart (Figure 1).

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/create_cohort.R`](/R/create_cohort.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following helper files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](/R/functions.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from the script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/create_cohort.R")
```

## Loading the hospitalization files

The cohort starts from the two USRDS hospitalization files, which hold Medicare inpatient stays (decided in [#1](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/issues/1)). Only the dates and diagnosis columns are loaded.

Factor labels are switched off, so codes stay as plain text. usRds has no function that searches these files for codes, so each file is loaded whole and searched by the project's own code. The [usRds coverage](usrds-coverage.qmd) page records this as a gap (step 4).

```{r}
#| label: cohort-load-hospitalizations
#| eval: false
```

## Flagging cryptococcosis

Each record is flagged if any of its diagnosis columns holds a cryptococcosis code from the [code lists](code_lists.qmd). The search uses each file's own diagnosis columns.

```{r}
#| label: cohort-flag-records
#| eval: false
```

## Building stays

For people with any cryptococcosis record, all their hospitalization records are combined into stays, so a code on any record of a stay counts for the whole stay. Stays admitted from 2006 to 2016 are kept.

```{r}
#| label: cohort-build-stays
#| eval: false
```

## Transplant and birth dates

Each person's first transplant date comes from the USRDS transplant file, and their date of birth from the patients file. Both are loaded only for the people found above.

```{r}
#| label: cohort-load-transplants-patients
#| eval: false
```

## Physician claims

The paper excludes anyone with a cryptococcosis claim, "physician or hospitalization", before their first transplant. Hospital records are already loaded; physician and supplier claims come from `usRds::get_PS_ICD()`, for the people with a cryptococcosis stay, searched for the same cryptococcosis codes. That function matches codes exactly, so the run stops if the code list ever gains a prefix code that it would miss. usRds reaches these claims from 2006 onward only.

```{r}
#| label: cohort-physician-claims
#| eval: false
```

## Cohort candidates

One row per person, with their index stay and age. A single cryptococcosis claim of either kind, dated before the person's first transplant or before 2006, marks them for exclusion ([#4](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/issues/4)). One claim is enough: a clinician billing for cryptococcosis, even to rule it out, before transplant is a reason to doubt that the later episode is new, and studies that exclude an earlier condition usually take any single claim, because missing an earlier case matters more there than excluding a few people over a rule-out code [@chubak2012].

```{r}
#| label: cohort-candidates
#| eval: false
```

## Flowchart

The exclusions are applied in the plan's order, each as a flowchart step, so Figure 1 shows exactly how the cohort was reached:

1. people in the transplant file;
2. people with a cryptococcosis stay admitted on or after their first transplant (a stay admitted before it counts as cryptococcosis before transplant, which the paper excludes);
3. people with no cryptococcosis claim, hospital or physician, before their first transplant or before 2006;
4. people aged 18 to 90 at index admission.

The box labels are built from the study constants, so they can't fall out of step with the window or age range. The flowchart's final data is the cohort.

```{r}
#| label: cohort-flowchart
#| eval: false
```
